function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Could not localize the red block reliably enough to grasp it within the 20-decision budget. Five full closes (four at fingertip height ~0.81, one at pad height ~0.842) and a closing sweep all closed on air (gripper 0.013-0.058, never the ~0.35-0.5 of a held block); the red block remained visible 2-4 cm beside the gripper in the fixed cameras the entire time. The block was never picked up and the blue bowl placement was never attempted.", "hindsight": "The wrist camera is pitched well off vertical, so image-down mixes height and horizontal direction: the red block slid out of the wrist frame when descending and a cream-colored bowl interior reads as empty table, which repeatedly misled centering. Front and side fixed cameras have very different scales (front horizontal tracks -x at roughly 800 px/m; side vertical tracks -z at roughly 500 px/m) and the visible gripper body sits well above the fingertips, so pixel offsets from the gripper blob overstate horizontal offsets by several cm. Gripper closing takes ~80 steps while a gripperless Cartesian move runs only ~2 steps, and the position servo converges exponentially with several mm of lag, so target accuracy must be built into long (gripper-delta-driven) motions, not repeated re-issued targets. A 2.5 cm block appears to need the TCP near z~0.83-0.84 so the pads, not the thin tips, align with it."}
